name: Oregano

companions.note: Classic companion — oregano repels aphids and spider mites; both thrive in full sun
Oregano deters cabbage moths; aromatic herbs generally benefit brassicas
Both attract pollinators; create a strong beneficial insect habitat together

pnw_notes: One of the most drought-tolerant herbs in the garden — thrives in PNW dry summers. Flavor is most intense just before flowering in midsummer; cut back by half after first flowering to encourage a second flush. Semi-evergreen in zone 8b; may die back to the crown in a hard freeze but returns vigorously in spring. Greek and Italian varieties have stronger flavor than common oregano.

frost_hardiness.notes: Reliably perennial in zone 8b. May die back to the crown in a hard freeze but returns vigorously in spring.

planting_windows.notes: Spring transplant preferred; establish before summer drought sets in
Fall planting works well in zone 8b — roots establish in cool, moist soil
Peak flavor June–August just before and during bloom; dry easily for winter use
